headline: The change is directionally good, but it introduces a Node-runtime compatibility trap that can hard-fail local workflows.

findings.point: tools/i18n/translate.mjs:75 calls process.loadEnvFile() unguarded; on Node versions where this API is absent, the script throws TypeError and exits before any translation logic.
tools/i18n/translate.mjs:86 loads .env for every mode (including --check); this adds an unnecessary startup dependency on local filesystem/env parsing for a mode that may not need credentials.

suggestions: Feature-detect process.loadEnvFile and throw a clear, single-line error with the minimum supported Node version (or fallback parser) instead of raw TypeError.
Add tests for .env behaviors: missing file no-op, malformed file hard-fail, and existing process.env values not overwritten.
Load .env only in modes that actually need API credentials, or document why --check intentionally loads it.

headline: Safe addition of local .env loading for translation API key; no exploitable path introduced by the diff.
suggestions: Ensure .env is listed in .gitignore to prevent accidental commit of secrets.

headline: loadDotEnv will crash on any Node <20.6 or when .env is present but unreadable.

findings.point: tools/i18n/translate.mjs:80: process.loadEnvFile(path) called with no existence check; TypeError on older Node is not ENOENT so it propagates
tools/i18n/translate.mjs:71: loadDotEnv runs before any arg parsing or version guard, so `npm run translate` fails immediately in CI or pinned Node 18/20.5
tools/i18n/translate.mjs:76: only ENOENT is swallowed; EACCES, EPERM, or malformed .env will still throw and abort the entire script

suggestions: use dotenv or a try/catch around the whole call with explicit version check
